problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=-{x}^{3}{y}^{2}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$ 

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the expression $f(x,y)=-2{x}^{2}{y}^{2}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/c35c98904d2a0d0d6d49c582cd9f9dba9d96e91ae0da5deb2d329f38f77532e3.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/9340582eaad37c4ce1e0c8cbcdce48faec1e36c3c05adbedd61aa2de7168fd2f.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-2{x}^{2}$ | ${y}^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |

 
Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040514/assets/692942228da99b0e5e871d8b293009d9226f900df417a20f7035f7bab5ae3a63.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>0$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | $-$ | $-$ |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
